title: Slice-based activation priority ladder and emergency fallback scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for a slice-first "priority ladder" approach to phased activation (canary + A/B) and a compact emergency fallback playbook focused on telemetry-driven gates, cost-aware hedging, and minimal human toil.

Scope / audience:
- Product, Console, SRE, Observability, Solutions Eng
- Intended to feed into: rollout orchestration templates, console UI for activation, and oncall runbooks

High-level idea (one-liner):
Define an ordered ladder of traffic slices to activate. Each rung has explicit, simple telemetry gates (health + quality + cost), an expected time window, and a pre-wired fallback action that is low-latency to execute. Prefer simple, automatable gates over combinatorial heuristics.

Priority ladder sketch (example):
1) internal-dev-only (rung 0) — smoke tests, synthetic generation. 10–15m. Gate: success rate > 98% on deterministic prompts. Fallback: revert config to baseline model.
2) stewarded-microcohort (rung 1) — internal employees + trust cohort (~0.1% traffic). 1–4 hours. Gates: latency p95 < 300ms, error rate < 0.5%, model-quality drift (BLEU/QA) within threshold. Fallback: throttle to 0% and route steward cohort to baseline variant. Alert: page steward owner.
3) segmented-beta (rung 2) — opt-in beta customers, low exposure (1–3%). 24h. Gates: business metric deltas within safety band, cost per 1k tokens not > 1.25x baseline. Fallback: route beta to cheaper quantized variant + enable prefix caching.
4) regional-rollout (rung 3) — single region, 10–20% of region. 48–72h. Gates: cross-region latency delta < 10%, error budget consumption < 30% of daily target, cohort uplift > 0 or neutral. Fallback: dynamic downgrade to a compatible smaller model + traffic split to hosted pool.
5) full-activation (rung 4) — ramp to 100% following a linear schedule. Ongoing monitoring.

Telemetry taxonomy (minimal set to check automatically):
- Availability: 5xx rate, connection failures, token streaming failures
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 request durations (decode vs total), KV cache hit ratio
- Cost signals: cost-per-1k-tokens, GPU utilization (per instance), batching occupancy
- Quality signals: prompt-pair eval score (pre-specified testset), user-sentiment proxy (NL classifier), rerank loss if present
- Behavioral checks: hallucination-rate heuristic (entity halluc detection), toxic content flags
- Drift checks: prompt-anchored perplexity shift, top-k token distribution shift

Gating logic (principles):
- Gates are monotonic and conservative: when multiple gates exist, failing any gate should pause progression.
- Use tiered tolerances: early rungs allow larger quality variance but tight availability/latency; later rungs tighten quality bands.
- Timebox evaluation windows to avoid noisy early stops (e.g., 30m rolling + 95% CI for metrics).
- Prefer deterministic synthetic probes that exercise critical paths (e.g., long-context, function-calls, streaming).

Cost-aware fallback patterns (fast, automatable):
- Soft downgrade: switch traffic to a lower-cost quantized model variant serving in same infra. (Requires pre-warmed pool)
- Graceful throttling: reduce experimental slice to X% and keep user-visible behavior intact with cached responses for repeat prefixes
- Regional shift: route experimental traffic across regions where capacity is underutilized and cheaper (if latency budget allows)
- Hybrid fallback: for latency-sensitive calls, route to baseline low-latency smaller model; for background work, keep experiments enabled at lower throughput

Operational run actions (operator checklist):
Pre-activation checklist:
- Confirm model variant compatibility across fallback variants (schema, tokens, function signatures)
- Pre-warm fallback pools and verify health endpoints
- Publish experiment config in console with explicit owner and SLA
- Create a lightweight alert policy (pager thresholds + Slack channel)
- Define synthetic probe set and commit to the repo (link above)

During activation checklist:
- Monitor synthetic probes + primary telemetry dashboard live
- Observe human-sampled qualitative checks (steward checklist) for first 2 hours
- Run quick A/B metric evaluation (precomputed scripts) at 4h window
- If a gate fails: execute fallback action (single-button in console) and annotate change in experiment log

Post-activation:
- 24h retrospective on signal stability and business metric delta
- If lifted to full: schedule 7d and 30d quality regression checks
- Archive experiment config and produce short teardown summary

A/B cohort sizing heuristics (practical):
- Start with microcohort approach for high-risk behavioral changes: n_min = max(1000 unique users, 0.1% daily active)
- For metric-sensitive experiments: compute power for delta detection (use approximate baseline var from last 30d). Guidelines: detect 2–3% relative change => need ~20–60k users depending on variance.
- Avoid large all-at-once splits for LLM features that cascade (rerankers, multi-turn dialog). Prefer progressive increments: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%

Synthetic probes guidance (examples):
- Short-answer factual (precision-sensitive)
- Long-context summarization (memory + truncation behavior)
- Function-call correctness (special token/formatting)
- Streaming under misordered chunks (simulate connection issues)

Quick formulas to embed in console UI: (for operator)
- Effective cost delta = (cost_per_token_exp - cost_per_token_base) / cost_per_token_base
- Latency headroom = target_p95 - observed_p95

Automation suggestions (low effort, high value):
- Auto-annotate experiment log with first-failure reason using rule templates (e.g., latency vs hallucination)
- Pre-bake buttons: Pause, Reduce-to-quantized, Route-to-baseline, Region-shift. Each action executes a small orchestration runbook.
- Keep a single source-of-truth repo for probe sets and threshold configs.

Open questions / TODO (working list):
- What is the canonical definition of hallucination we use for auto gating? Need to standardize metric and threshold. (Owner: Dana)
- How to surface cost-hedging options in a way that non-infra teams can safely click them? Need RBAC + simulation mode. (Owner: Marcus)
- Should we allow automated fallback triggers to act without human ack at rung >=2? Pro: speed. Con: noise / false positives. Suggest: enable but restrict to low-impact hedges only.
- Integration: wire console action buttons to dedicated autoscaling policies to ensure fallback pools are actually pre-warmed. (Engineering: infra + serving-runtime)

Incident mini-runbook (when a gate trips):
1) Console raises experiment alarm and posts summary in #rollouts channel (auto-post includes failing metric, last 5 traces).
2) If latch is manual: steward assesses within 10m; if auto-enabled: execute the configured fallback.
3) Post-fallback: run a lightweight root-cause checklist (a) capacity/queue backlog, (b) decoding errors, (c) model drift on eval set, (d) external dependency outage.
4) If fallback did not mitigate: escalate to SRE oncall and prepare a rollback to baseline.

Notes to self / brainstorming fragments (informal):
- Could use a single numeric risk score combining latency, cost, and quality percentiles to rank slices automatically for parallel activations. But risk of obscuring root cause.
- Consider an "experiment dry-run" mode that simulates projected cost delta and queues without flipping traffic. Useful for sales/legal reviews.
- We need a small canonical deck for GTM + Support explaining what a fallback means for customers. Keep it <3 slides.

References and links:
- Experiment probe repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/probes (wip)
- Related playbook (draft): CONFLUENCE: Experiment-ops/safety-channeling (see linked_artifacts above)
- Jira epic for orchestration buttons: RINF-1276

Quick meeting agenda to align teams (30m):
- 5m: overview of ladder concept and motivation
- 10m: walk through sample activation for model X (who does what at each rung)
- 10m: confirm fallback actions and automation scope (who owns pre-warm)
- 5m: assign next steps & owners

Owner notes: Priya — keep this as a scratchpad until we converge on thresholds; next step is to prototype console buttons for the three hedges (quantized downgrade, throttle, region shift) and demo with steward cohort.

End of scratchpad.
